title: C# Core Concepts & OOP
description: Architect-level understanding of C# types, polymorphism, reusable abstractions, and object-oriented design.

topics.title: Value Types vs Reference Types
topics.summary: Value and reference types differ in assignment and identity semantics, not by a universal stack-versus-heap rule.

topics.title: Struct vs Class vs Record
topics.summary: Classes model identity, structs model copied values, and records add value-oriented equality to either reference or value types.

topics.title: When to Use a Class, Struct, or Record
topics.summary: Choose types from domain semantics first, then validate allocation and copying costs with measurement.

topics.title: Boxing and Unboxing
topics.summary: Boxing wraps a value type as an object/interface value; unboxing extracts a value of the exact value type.

topics.title: ref, out, and in Parameters
topics.summary: These modifiers pass a variable by reference with distinct initialization and mutation rules.

topics.title: Abstract Class vs Interface
topics.summary: An interface defines a substitutable capability contract; an abstract class can also own shared state and implementation.

topics.title: Generics vs Object-Based APIs
topics.summary: Generics preserve the element type; object-based APIs erase it and move checking and conversion work to runtime.

topics.title: Generics & Variance
topics.summary: Generics parameterize reusable code with compile-time type safety; variance allows safe conversions between selected constructed types.

topics.title: Overloading vs Overriding
topics.summary: Overloading selects among same-named signatures at compile time; overriding replaces inherited virtual behavior at runtime.

topics.title: virtual, override, and new
topics.summary: virtual opens a polymorphic method slot, override participates in that slot, and new hides a member by name.

topics.title: Four OOP Pillars in a Working Design
topics.summary: Encapsulation, abstraction, inheritance, and polymorphism are complementary techniques for controlling change.

topics.title: SRP: Single Responsibility Principle
topics.summary: A module should have one cohesive responsibility—one primary reason to change—not merely one method.

topics.title: OCP: Open/Closed Principle
topics.summary: Stable code should accept new supported behavior through extension points rather than repeated edits to a central decision block.

topics.title: LSP: Liskov Substitution Principle
topics.summary: A subtype must honor the behavioral promises clients rely on when using the base contract.

topics.title: ISP: Interface Segregation Principle
topics.summary: Clients should depend on focused interfaces containing only operations they actually need.

topics.title: DIP: Dependency Inversion Principle
topics.summary: High-level policy and low-level details should depend on stable abstractions, with implementation details kept at the edge.

topics.title: Dependency Injection and Its Value
topics.summary: Dependency injection supplies an object’s collaborators from outside instead of having the object construct concrete dependencies itself.

topics.title: Extension Methods
topics.summary: An extension method adds callable syntax to a type without modifying or inheriting from that type.

topics.title: Delegates, Events, Func, and Action
topics.summary: Delegates are type-safe method references; Func and Action are standard delegate shapes, while events control publisher notifications.

title: C# Coding & Algorithms
description: Practice data structures, complexity analysis, and interview-style implementation problems.

topics.title: Reverse a String
topics.summary: Reverse a string by converting it to a mutable character buffer and swapping characters from the two ends.

topics.title: Reverse Words in a Sentence
topics.summary: Split a sentence into words and emit them in reverse order without reversing the letters inside each word.

topics.title: Palindrome Check with Two Pointers
topics.summary: Compare matching characters from both ends, skipping characters the problem defines as irrelevant.

topics.title: Anagram Check with Character Counts
topics.summary: Two strings are anagrams when their normalized character frequencies match exactly.

topics.title: First Non-Repeating Character
topics.summary: Count characters in one pass, then scan in the original order to find the first character with count one.

topics.title: Two Sum with a Dictionary
topics.summary: Find two array positions whose values sum to a target by remembering values already seen.

topics.title: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters
topics.summary: Use a sliding window to find the longest contiguous substring whose characters are all unique.

topics.title: Binary Search in a Sorted Array
topics.summary: Find a target in a sorted array by repeatedly discarding the half that cannot contain it.

topics.title: Reverse a Linked List & Detect Cycles
topics.summary: Reverse a singly linked list in place, then use Floyd’s tortoise-and-hare algorithm to determine whether a list loops back on itself.

topics.title: LRU Cache
topics.summary: An LRU (least recently used) cache keeps a bounded set of entries and evicts the entry that has gone longest without use.

title: Async Programming, Tasks, Threads & Memory
description: Design scalable asynchronous code, protect shared state, and diagnose managed-memory and resource-lifetime problems.

topics.title: Asynchronous vs Synchronous Work
topics.summary: Synchronous calls wait inline; asynchronous operations let the caller make progress while an operation is pending.

topics.title: Task vs Thread
topics.summary: A Task models an operation’s completion and outcome; a Thread is an operating-system execution resource.

topics.title: .NET Thread Pool
topics.summary: The thread pool reuses worker threads for short-running work and coordinates queued callbacks and continuations.

topics.title: What Happens Inside an Async Method
topics.summary: An async method runs synchronously until it reaches an incomplete awaitable, then returns control and resumes later.

topics.title: Compiler State Machine and Await
topics.summary: The compiler transforms an async method into a state machine that stores progress across suspension points.

topics.title: Task vs Task.Run
topics.summary: Task represents work or completion; Task.Run schedules a delegate on the thread pool.

topics.title: Task.WhenAll vs Task.WhenAny
topics.summary: WhenAll completes after all supplied tasks complete; WhenAny completes when one task completes.

topics.title: Async Methods Without Await
topics.summary: An async method with no await runs synchronously and may add a redundant state machine or task wrapper.

topics.title: Consequences of an Unawaited Async Call
topics.summary: An unawaited Task is unobserved by the caller: the operation still runs, but ordering, errors, and completion are no longer coordinated.

topics.title: ConfigureAwait(false)
topics.summary: ConfigureAwait(false) tells an await not to require resuming on the captured synchronization context.

topics.title: Thread Safety and Race Conditions
topics.summary: Thread-safe code preserves invariants when multiple execution flows access shared state concurrently.

topics.title: lock vs SemaphoreSlim
topics.summary: lock synchronizes synchronous critical sections; SemaphoreSlim controls concurrent entry and supports asynchronous waiting.

topics.title: Thread Pool Starvation
topics.summary: Thread-pool starvation occurs when queued work cannot obtain worker threads promptly, often because workers are blocked.

topics.title: .NET Memory Management
topics.summary: Managed memory allocation and reclamation are runtime-managed, while resource ownership and object reachability remain application responsibilities.

topics.title: .NET Garbage Collector
topics.summary: The garbage collector finds unreachable managed objects and reuses their memory, with runtime strategies tuned for common allocation patterns.

topics.title: Gen 0, Gen 1, and Gen 2
topics.summary: Generations group managed objects by survival history so the GC can collect short-lived objects more frequently and cheaply.

topics.title: IDisposable, IAsyncDisposable, and Finalizers
topics.summary: Dispose provides deterministic resource cleanup; finalization is a nondeterministic fallback for directly owned unmanaged resources.

topics.title: Diagnosing Memory Leaks
topics.summary: A managed memory leak is often unintended retention: objects remain reachable after the application no longer needs them.

title: ASP.NET Core Web API
description: Design maintainable HTTP APIs with explicit controller semantics, pipeline behavior, validation, and versioned contracts.

topics.title: HTTP Method Semantics
topics.summary: HTTP methods communicate the intended operation and whether it is safe or idempotent, independent of how an endpoint is named.

topics.title: Common HTTP Status Codes
topics.summary: Status codes classify success, client-side request problems, and server failures; 400, 401, 403, 404, 409, and 500 have distinct meanings.

topics.title: ASP.NET Core Request Pipeline
topics.summary: The ordered middleware pipeline surrounds endpoint execution, so ordering determines which components can observe and affect a request.

topics.title: Middleware & Custom Middleware
topics.summary: Middleware is an HTTP delegate that can inspect, transform, short-circuit, or delegate request processing.

topics.title: Controller vs ControllerBase
topics.summary: Controller extends ControllerBase with view and page-oriented capabilities; ControllerBase is the smaller choice for HTTP APIs.

topics.title: ControllerBase Advantages
topics.summary: ControllerBase gives API controllers MVC request, binding, validation, and response helpers without the view-rendering features of Controller.

topics.title: Controllers vs Minimal APIs
topics.summary: Controllers and Minimal APIs are two ASP.NET Core endpoint styles that share routing, dependency injection, authorization, and HTTP semantics.

topics.title: Purpose of [ApiController]
topics.summary: [ApiController] opts MVC controllers into conventions that make API binding and client-error behavior more predictable.

topics.title: Controllers Without [ApiController]
topics.summary: A controller without [ApiController] can still serve an API, but it does not receive that attribute’s API-specific conventions automatically.

topics.title: API Data Transfer Objects (DTOs)
topics.summary: DTOs define intentional API input and output contracts, decoupled from persistence entities and internal domain models.

topics.title: Model Validation
topics.summary: Model validation checks bound input against structural constraints, while application logic separately enforces business invariants.

topics.title: ASP.NET Core Response Result Types
topics.summary: Action return types communicate whether an endpoint returns a representation, several HTTP outcomes, or a framework-level result.

topics.title: Dependency Injection & Service Lifetimes
topics.summary: Transient, scoped, and singleton lifetimes define how long a resolved service instance is reused and who disposes it.

topics.title: Middleware vs MVC Filters
topics.summary: Middleware wraps the application request pipeline; MVC filters run inside MVC execution and have action or result context.

topics.title: Global Exception Handling
topics.summary: A global exception boundary logs unexpected failures and returns a stable, safe error contract rather than leaking implementation details.

topics.title: API Versioning
topics.summary: API versioning manages incompatible contract evolution while clients migrate at different speeds.

topics.title: Logging & Timing Middleware
topics.summary: Request instrumentation correlates HTTP outcomes and elapsed time with structured logs and distributed traces.

title: API Concurrency & Resilience
description: Handle competing edits, retries, and failures without corrupting data or duplicating effects.

topics.title: Data Concurrency
topics.summary: Data concurrency is the behavior of overlapping operations that read or change shared state.

topics.title: Concurrent Edits & Lost Updates
topics.summary: A lost update occurs when a later save overwrites changes made after the editor loaded its original copy.

topics.title: Optimistic vs Pessimistic Concurrency
topics.summary: Optimistic concurrency detects a conflict when committing; pessimistic concurrency acquires a lock to exclude competing work.

topics.title: SQL Server RowVersion & EF Core
topics.summary: SQL Server rowversion is an automatically changing binary version stamp that EF Core can use to detect a stale update.

topics.title: Handling Concurrent Edits in an API
topics.summary: An API should define how a detected stale update is communicated and how a client can recover without overwriting newer state.

topics.title: Idempotent HTTP Methods
topics.summary: HTTP defines PUT and DELETE as idempotent in intended effect, and GET, HEAD, OPTIONS, and TRACE as safe and therefore idempotent.

topics.title: Request Idempotency & Idempotency Keys
topics.summary: An idempotent operation has the same intended effect when the same request is repeated, which makes uncertain network retries safer.

topics.title: PUT vs PATCH
topics.summary: PUT conventionally replaces a resource representation; PATCH applies a defined partial modification.

topics.title: PUT: Avoiding Unnecessary Database Writes
topics.summary: A PUT request can be idempotent even if the server writes each time; avoiding needless writes is a separate optimization and side-effect concern.

topics.title: Preventing Duplicate Orders & Payments
topics.summary: Duplicate-sensitive business operations need durable deduplication across retries, concurrent requests, and downstream failures.

topics.title: Error Status Codes for APIs
topics.summary: Status codes distinguish invalid input, missing authentication, denied access, stale state, and unexpected server failure.

topics.title: Standard API Error Responses
topics.summary: A standard error body gives clients stable machine-readable classification without exposing internal implementation details.

topics.title: ProblemDetails in ASP.NET Core
topics.summary: ProblemDetails is ASP.NET Core’s model for producing interoperable error documents based on the Problem Details standard.

topics.title: Centralized Exception Handling
topics.summary: Centralized exception handling turns unhandled failures into consistent, safe API responses while preserving operational diagnostics.

title: Angular
description: Architect Angular applications with deliberate state, HTTP, routing, forms, and rendering choices.

topics.title: Angular Lifecycle Hooks
topics.summary: Lifecycle hooks mark specific points in a component or directive’s creation, input processing, rendering, and destruction.

topics.title: Component Communication
topics.summary: Communication mechanisms should follow component ownership and data direction, from direct parent-child contracts to shared state services.

topics.title: Lazy Loading
topics.summary: Lazy loading defers feature code until navigation or explicit demand, improving initial payload at the cost of later loading work.

topics.title: Route Guards
topics.summary: Route guards express client-side navigation policy and user experience; they never replace server-side authorization.

topics.title: Observable vs Promise
topics.summary: Observable and Promise represent different asynchronous contracts: a single eventual result versus a lazy, composable sequence.

topics.title: Subject vs BehaviorSubject
topics.summary: Choose a multicast primitive by its late-subscriber contract, not simply because a value is shared.

topics.title: forkJoin vs combineLatest vs merge
topics.summary: These operators combine sources with different timing contracts: final values, latest snapshots, or interleaved emissions.

topics.title: Call APIs Simultaneously
topics.summary: Compose independent requests concurrently, and choose a join operator whose completion and failure semantics match the page contract.

topics.title: Cancel In-Flight HTTP Requests
topics.summary: Cancel obsolete client-side work to avoid stale rendering and wasted resources, while distinguishing client abort from server rollback.

topics.title: HTTP Interceptors
topics.summary: Functional interceptors provide an ordered shared pipeline for cross-cutting request and response policies.

topics.title: Handle API Errors
topics.summary: Treat HTTP failures as typed application states, preserving useful diagnostics while presenting safe, actionable user feedback.

topics.title: Attach JWTs to Requests Safely
topics.summary: Attach an access token only to requests that are intended for the trusted API, and keep token storage and transport risks explicit.

topics.title: Token Expiration and Refresh
topics.summary: Handle expiry as an authentication lifecycle with race control, bounded replay, and secure failure behavior.

topics.title: Template-Driven vs Reactive Forms
topics.summary: Both approaches use Angular forms controls; they differ mainly in where the form model and validation logic are authored.

topics.title: Change Detection
topics.summary: Change detection synchronizes template bindings with application state; performance depends on what gets checked and how state changes are observed.

topics.title: Default vs OnPush
topics.summary: Default and OnPush differ in when a view is eligible for checking, not in whether Angular can update it.

topics.title: Angular Signals
topics.summary: Signals provide synchronous reactive state with tracked reads, derived values, and controlled side effects.

topics.title: Signals vs RxJS
topics.summary: Signals model current synchronous state; RxJS models asynchronous sequences, time, cancellation, and event composition.

topics.title: State Management in Large Applications
topics.summary: Large-app state architecture is a set of ownership and consistency decisions, not a requirement to put every value in one global store.

topics.title: Angular Performance
topics.summary: Optimize measured user-visible bottlenecks across rendering, network, bundle, and memory rather than chasing a single framework metric.

title: API Security & Auth
description: Protect APIs through layered identity, least-privilege authorization, browser controls, safe data handling, and abuse resistance.

topics.title: Securing an ASP.NET Core API
topics.summary: API security is a layered system of transport protection, trusted identity, authorization, input and data safety, resilience, and operational response.

topics.title: Authentication vs Authorization
topics.summary: Authentication establishes a trusted identity; authorization decides what that identity may do to a specific operation or resource.

topics.title: JWT vs OAuth 2.0 vs OpenID Connect
topics.summary: JWT is a token format, OAuth 2.0 is an authorization framework, and OpenID Connect is an authentication layer built on OAuth 2.0.

topics.title: OAuth 2.0 Authorization
topics.summary: OAuth 2.0 lets a client obtain limited access to a protected resource without sharing the resource owner’s password with that client.

topics.title: OpenID Connect & User Sign-In
topics.summary: OpenID Connect adds an interoperable identity layer to OAuth 2.0 so a client can validate a user authentication result.

topics.title: JWT Access Token Validation
topics.summary: An API must validate a bearer access token’s cryptographic and protocol constraints before it trusts claims or authorizes a request.

topics.title: Role vs Policy Authorization
topics.summary: Roles provide coarse identity groupings; policies express named requirements and can combine claims, roles, and custom handlers.

topics.title: Microsoft Entra ID & User Sign-In
topics.summary: Microsoft Entra ID is an identity platform that can authenticate users and issue protocol tokens for registered applications and APIs.

topics.title: Integrating Entra ID with an ASP.NET Core API
topics.summary: An ASP.NET Core API integrates with Entra as a resource server: validate bearer access tokens for the API, then apply application authorization.

topics.title: Service-to-Service Authentication
topics.summary: Workload identity authenticates an application or service without pretending it is an end user.

topics.title: CORS & Browser Preflight
topics.summary: CORS is a browser-enforced cross-origin response-sharing policy, not authentication or protection against non-browser clients.

topics.title: Access Tokens vs Refresh Tokens
topics.summary: Access tokens are presented to resource APIs; refresh tokens are high-value credentials used with the authorization server to obtain renewed access.

topics.title: Token Expiration & Key Rotation
topics.summary: Expiration bounds how long a credential is accepted; rotation replaces credentials or signing keys while preserving controlled continuity.

topics.title: Frontend Token Storage
topics.summary: Browser token storage is a threat-model trade-off: script-readable storage exposes tokens to XSS, while cookie-based sessions require CSRF protections.

topics.title: Secure Password Storage
topics.summary: Passwords should be stored as salted, deliberately expensive one-way password hashes, never as plaintext or reversibly encrypted values.

topics.title: API Keys
topics.summary: An API key identifies or gates a client integration but is a bearer secret and usually does not provide end-user identity or fine-grained authorization.

topics.title: SQL Injection Prevention
topics.summary: SQL injection occurs when untrusted input changes query structure; parameterization keeps values data rather than executable SQL.

topics.title: XSS & CSRF
topics.summary: XSS attacks run attacker-controlled script in a user’s browser; CSRF tricks a browser into sending an authenticated action using ambient credentials.

topics.title: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)
topics.summary: SSRF abuses a server feature that fetches a caller-influenced destination, potentially crossing network trust boundaries.

topics.title: Broken Object-Level Authorization (BOLA)
topics.summary: BOLA occurs when an API checks who the caller is but fails to check whether they may access the specific record they requested.

topics.title: Mass Assignment & Over-Posting
topics.summary: Mass assignment occurs when an API binds untrusted request fields directly to a domain or persistence object, allowing callers to set fields they should not control.

topics.title: Credential Stuffing & Brute-Force Defense
topics.summary: Credential stuffing reuses leaked username/password pairs, while brute-force attacks repeatedly guess credentials; layered controls limit account takeover and abuse.

topics.title: API Rate Limiting
topics.summary: Rate limiting bounds request consumption to protect service capacity and fairness, but it does not replace authorization or broader abuse defenses.

title: SQL Server
description: Write analytical queries and reason about indexes, transactions, concurrency, and production performance.

topics.title: SQL Query Processing Order
topics.summary: A SELECT statement has a logical binding order: FROM, ON, JOIN, WHERE, GROUP BY, GROUPING SETS/CUBE/ROLLUP, HAVING, SELECT, DISTINCT, ORDER BY, then TOP/OFFSET-FETCH. FROM establishes input rowsets; ON evaluates the join predicate; JOIN combines matches (and preserves unmatched rows for outer joins); WHERE filters individual rows; GROUP BY forms groups; HAVING filters groups; SELECT computes output expressions and aliases; DISTINCT removes duplicate projected rows; ORDER BY orders output; TOP limits it.

topics.title: INNER JOIN vs LEFT JOIN
topics.summary: INNER JOIN returns rows with matching join keys on both sides. LEFT JOIN preserves every left-side row and returns NULLs for right-side columns when no match exists.

topics.title: CTE vs Temporary Table vs Table Variable
topics.summary: A CTE names a query expression for one following statement; #temp tables are session-scoped tempdb tables; table variables are variables backed by tempdb with table-like structure and narrower scope.

topics.title: Stored Procedure vs Function
topics.summary: A stored procedure is an executable database routine that can accept parameters, return result sets/output parameters, and perform data modifications. A function returns a scalar or table value and is designed to participate in expressions or FROM clauses, subject to SQL Server function restrictions.

topics.title: Prevent SQL Injection
topics.summary: SQL injection occurs when untrusted input is concatenated into SQL syntax, allowing input to alter the intended command or predicate.

topics.title: Highest Salary Per Department
topics.summary: The maximum salary per department can be returned as a value, or with the employee row or rows that achieve it.

topics.title: Employees Above Their Department Average
topics.summary: A per-department comparison evaluates each employee salary against an aggregate calculated for that employee’s department.

topics.title: ROW_NUMBER vs RANK vs DENSE_RANK
topics.summary: These window ranking functions assign positions within an ordered partition. ROW_NUMBER assigns a unique sequence; RANK gives ties the same rank and leaves gaps; DENSE_RANK gives ties the same rank without gaps.

topics.title: Find the Second-Highest Salary
topics.summary: Second-highest can mean the second distinct salary value, or the employee row in second place. Those meanings differ when salaries tie.

topics.title: Department-Wise Top Three Salaries
topics.summary: Top-N-per-group returns a limited or ranked set of employees independently within each department. A window function computes a rank without collapsing employee rows.

topics.title: Find Duplicate Rows by Business Key
topics.summary: A duplicate is a repeated business key, not necessarily a byte-for-byte identical database row. The key might be a normalized email, external reference, or composite of several columns.

topics.title: Delete Duplicates While Keeping One
topics.summary: A deterministic keeper rule selects exactly one surviving row per duplicate business key; other rows become deletion candidates.

topics.title: Clustered and Nonclustered Indexes
topics.summary: A clustered index is the table’s rowstore B-tree whose leaf level contains the data rows; a table has at most one. A nonclustered index is a separate B-tree with key columns and a row locator (clustered key or RID), and a table may have many.

topics.title: How Indexes Speed Queries
topics.summary: A B-tree index narrows the rows that must be visited for selective predicates and can provide ordered rows or cover all columns needed by a query.

topics.title: Read SQL Server Execution Plans
topics.summary: An execution plan is the optimizer’s chosen physical strategy: operators and data flow used to execute a query. An estimated plan contains estimates; an actual plan adds runtime observations such as actual rows and executions.

topics.title: Slow Query Optimization Method
topics.summary: Query optimization is a measured process of identifying the dominant cost (I/O, CPU, waits, blocking, network, or client processing) and changing the query, index, statistics, or workload safely.

topics.title: ACID Transaction Guarantees
topics.summary: ACID describes Atomicity (all-or-nothing), Consistency (valid states/invariants), Isolation (concurrent work behaves according to isolation rules), and Durability (committed work survives failures according to configured guarantees).

topics.title: Transaction Isolation Levels
topics.summary: Isolation defines what changes a transaction can observe and which concurrent anomalies are prevented. SQL Server offers READ UNCOMMITTED, READ COMMITTED, REPEATABLE READ, SERIALIZABLE, and SNAPSHOT; READ COMMITTED SNAPSHOT (RCSI) is a database option that provides statement-level versioned reads.

topics.title: Concurrent Updates to the Same Row
topics.summary: Concurrent writes to one row contend for locks or encounter optimistic concurrency conflicts. A later write may wait, overwrite earlier values, or fail based on transaction and application design.

topics.title: Deadlocks and Safe Recovery
topics.summary: A deadlock is a cycle of transactions, each holding a resource needed by another. SQL Server detects the cycle and chooses a victim; error 1205 means that victim transaction was rolled back.

topics.title: Diagnose SQL Server Errors by Cause
topics.summary: SQL Server error numbers identify a failure category, but the constraint, statement, transaction state, and surrounding context explain the root cause. 2601 and 2627 indicate unique-key violations; 547 indicates a CHECK or FOREIGN KEY constraint conflict; 1205 means the transaction was selected as a deadlock victim.

title: EF Core, Testing & Real Project Scenarios
description: Build efficient data access, test meaningful boundaries, and diagnose production systems with evidence.

topics.title: Entity Framework Core Fundamentals
topics.summary: Entity Framework Core (EF Core) is a .NET object-relational mapper (ORM): it maps .NET entity types and LINQ queries to relational schema and SQL through a database provider. DbContext is a unit-of-work and identity map that coordinates querying, change tracking, and saving.

topics.title: Code First vs Database First
topics.summary: Code First treats the EF model and migrations as the schema-evolution source of truth. Database First starts from an existing database and scaffolds entity types and DbContext from its schema; the generated code can be refreshed as the database changes.

topics.title: Tracking vs No-Tracking Queries
topics.summary: A tracking query registers materialized entities in DbContext’s change tracker, which records state and original values for SaveChanges. A no-tracking query materializes results without registering them for normal updates; identity resolution controls whether repeated keys share an instance.

topics.title: Eager, Lazy, and Explicit Loading
topics.summary: Eager loading fetches related data as part of the original query using Include/ThenInclude or projection. Lazy loading loads a navigation on access, commonly through proxies. Explicit loading deliberately issues a later query through the entry API.

topics.title: Detect and Eliminate the N+1 Problem
topics.summary: N+1 is a query pattern where one query loads N parent records and subsequent navigation access issues roughly one additional query per parent.

topics.title: EF Core Query Optimization
topics.summary: EF Core query optimization aligns the LINQ expression, generated SQL, indexes, result shape, and database plan with the workload. Deferred IQueryable composition runs at the database only when materialized or enumerated.

topics.title: Mock vs Stub vs Fake
topics.summary: A stub supplies predefined answers; a mock records or verifies expected interactions; a fake is a working simplified implementation (for example, an in-memory repository) that preserves a useful contract.

topics.title: Unit Testing Application Logic
topics.summary: A unit test verifies a focused unit of behavior with controlled inputs and collaborators, typically without booting the web host or connecting to a production-like database.

topics.title: Integration Testing APIs and Persistence
topics.summary: An integration test exercises multiple real components across a boundary, such as HTTP routing, dependency injection, serialization, EF Core translation, and a relational database.

topics.title: Design Scalable Data-Backed APIs
topics.summary: A scalable API bounds work per request, isolates failures, manages concurrency and resources, and supports horizontal growth without relying on process-local state.

topics.title: Diagnose a Slow API in Production
topics.summary: Slow API diagnosis separates time spent in application code, database execution, network/dependency waits, queueing, serialization, and client transfer, then correlates a slow request with trace and resource evidence.

topics.title: Diagnose High CPU and Memory
topics.summary: High CPU can result from application hot loops, excessive serialization, query translation/materialization, contention, or garbage collection. High memory can be allocation pressure, large caches, unbounded buffers, or retained object graphs.

topics.title: Logging, Metrics, and Distributed Tracing
topics.summary: Logs record discrete events, metrics aggregate numerical time series, and traces connect spans across a request and its dependencies. Together they describe what happened, how often, and where latency accumulated.

topics.title: Database Failure Handling and Resilience
topics.summary: Database failure handling distinguishes transient connectivity/failover conditions, command timeouts, deadlocks, constraint conflicts, cancellation, and permanent configuration or schema errors.

topics.title: Production Incident Response
topics.summary: Incident handling is a structured process to reduce customer impact, preserve evidence, communicate status, restore service, and prevent recurrence.

title: Azure Cloud
description: Choose Azure compute, messaging, and identity services with explicit scaling, delivery, networking, and security decisions.

topics.title: App Service vs Functions vs Container Apps
topics.summary: Azure App Service, Azure Functions, and Azure Container Apps are managed compute platforms with different workload and operations boundaries.

topics.title: Azure Storage: Blob, Queue, and Files
topics.summary: Azure Storage provides distinct primitives: Blob for object data, Queue Storage for simple messages, and Azure Files for managed file shares.

topics.title: Key Vault & Managed Identity
topics.summary: Managed identity supplies an Azure workload identity; Key Vault controls access to stored secrets, keys, and certificates.

topics.title: Azure API Management & Gateway Policies
topics.summary: API Management provides a managed API gateway and developer-facing API lifecycle capabilities; policies apply controlled cross-cutting behavior at the gateway.

topics.title: Service Bus vs Event Hubs vs Event Grid
topics.summary: Azure Service Bus, Event Hubs, and Event Grid support distinct messaging semantics: durable work, retained event streams, and event notification routing.

topics.title: Azure Logic Apps & Workflow Automation
topics.summary: Logic Apps orchestrates connector-based workflows across services; it is best for integration and business processes, not as a substitute for every application service.

topics.title: Azure Monitoring, Availability & Cost
topics.summary: Production Azure architecture connects service health and application telemetry to measurable reliability, recovery, and cost objectives.

title: Microservices
description: Design service boundaries, communication, and failure recovery with explicit consistency and delivery guarantees.

topics.title: Monolith vs Microservices
topics.summary: A monolith packages an application as one deployable unit, while microservices split capabilities into separately owned and deployed services with explicit boundaries.

topics.title: Service Communication
topics.summary: Service communication is a contract and transport through which independently deployed components exchange commands, queries, or facts.

topics.title: Synchronous vs Asynchronous Communication
topics.summary: Synchronous request/response keeps the caller waiting for a result; asynchronous messaging lets sender and receiver progress at different times.

topics.title: Timeouts and Deadlines
topics.summary: A timeout bounds how long one operation waits; a deadline is the end-to-end time budget by which the whole request must complete.

topics.title: Retry Policy
topics.summary: A retry is another attempt after a classified transient failure; backoff spaces attempts, and jitter randomizes timing among callers.

topics.title: Circuit Breaker
topics.summary: A circuit breaker temporarily rejects calls to a dependency after a configured failure signal, then permits a limited recovery probe.

topics.title: API Gateway
topics.summary: An API gateway is a controlled client-facing entry point that routes requests and may handle cross-cutting edge concerns such as authentication, rate limiting, and protocol translation.

topics.title: Service Discovery
topics.summary: Service discovery resolves a logical service name to currently available instances or endpoints.

topics.title: RabbitMQ and Azure Service Bus Concepts
topics.summary: A message broker accepts messages and routes or stores them for consumers; RabbitMQ commonly uses exchanges, bindings, and queues, while Azure Service Bus provides queues and topics/subscriptions as managed messaging primitives.

topics.title: Event-Driven Architecture
topics.summary: Event-driven architecture uses events—immutable statements that something already happened—to notify interested consumers without requiring the producer to invoke each one.

topics.title: Duplicate Message Handling and Idempotency
topics.summary: A duplicate message is the same logical delivery processed more than once; an idempotent operation produces the same effective state when repeated with the same identity.

topics.title: Distributed Transactions
topics.summary: A distributed transaction attempts to commit changes across multiple resource managers as one atomic outcome, commonly through a coordinator and a protocol such as two-phase commit.

topics.title: Saga Pattern
topics.summary: A saga is a long-running business workflow made of local transactions, with forward actions and compensating actions to address later failure.

topics.title: Cross-Service Consistency
topics.summary: Cross-service consistency describes how independently committed data copies and service-owned states converge and what stale or intermediate state consumers may observe.

topics.title: Transactional Outbox
topics.summary: The transactional outbox stores the intent to publish alongside the business state change in the same local database transaction.

topics.title: Responding to a Downstream Outage
topics.summary: A downstream outage is any dependency becoming unavailable, slow, overloaded, or semantically unhealthy from this caller’s perspective.

topics.title: Failure Handling Across Services
topics.summary: Failure handling is the end-to-end policy for classifying errors, containing impact, recovering work, and communicating outcomes across service boundaries.

title: Design Patterns & SOLID
description: Apply patterns and design principles when they clarify responsibilities, variation, and testable boundaries.

topics.title: Patterns: What They Are and Why They Matter
topics.summary: A design pattern is a named, reusable arrangement of responsibilities and collaborations for a recurring design problem; it is guidance, not a library or a complete implementation.

topics.title: SOLID: Single Responsibility Principle
topics.summary: Single Responsibility Principle (SRP) says a module should have one coherent reason to change, often expressed as one actor or policy that owns its behavior.

topics.title: SOLID: Open/Closed Principle
topics.summary: Open/Closed Principle (OCP) says a component should support anticipated extension without requiring changes to stable existing code.

topics.title: SOLID: Liskov Substitution Principle
topics.summary: Liskov Substitution Principle (LSP) requires a subtype to remain usable wherever its base contract is expected without breaking promised behavior or strengthening preconditions.

topics.title: SOLID: Interface Segregation Principle
topics.summary: Interface Segregation Principle (ISP) says clients should not depend on operations they do not use; interfaces should represent cohesive client needs.

topics.title: SOLID: Dependency Inversion Principle
topics.summary: Dependency Inversion Principle (DIP) says high-level policy should not depend directly on low-level details; both should depend on abstractions owned around the policy.

topics.title: Dependency Injection Pattern
topics.summary: Dependency injection supplies an object’s required collaborators from outside rather than having the object construct or locate them itself.

topics.title: Factory Pattern
topics.summary: A factory centralizes object creation when construction depends on input, configuration, or a family of related products.

topics.title: Strategy Pattern: Shipping Rate Example
topics.summary: Strategy defines a family of interchangeable algorithms behind a common contract so a caller can select behavior without embedding each algorithm in its own conditional logic.

topics.title: Adapter Pattern
topics.summary: Adapter translates one interface or data model into another so incompatible components can collaborate without changing either component’s core contract.

topics.title: Decorator Pattern
topics.summary: Decorator wraps an object behind the same contract and adds behavior before or after delegating to the wrapped object.

topics.title: Observer Pattern
topics.summary: Observer establishes a one-to-many notification relationship: a subject publishes a change or event and interested observers react without the subject directly owning each observer’s work.

topics.title: Singleton Pattern and DI Lifetime
topics.summary: Singleton describes one shared instance for a defined application/container lifetime; in .NET, singleton DI registration is often preferable to a globally accessible static instance.

topics.title: Repository Pattern
topics.summary: A repository provides a domain-oriented boundary for retrieving and persisting aggregates while hiding persistence-specific details where that abstraction is valuable.

topics.title: Unit of Work Pattern
topics.summary: A unit of work coordinates a set of related changes and commits them as one local persistence transaction where the store supports it.

topics.title: CQRS
topics.summary: Command Query Responsibility Segregation separates operations that change state (commands) from operations that read and return data (queries).

topics.title: Patterns Used Together in Projects
topics.summary: Production systems commonly combine a few patterns around a use case: dependency injection assembles collaborators, a strategy selects policy, a repository may encapsulate domain queries, and a decorator adds cross-cutting behavior.

topics.title: Repository Pattern and Unit Testing
topics.summary: A unit test verifies a focused unit of behavior with controlled collaborators; a repository can provide a seam for application behavior, but it does not make database behavior correct by itself.

topics.title: Singleton Thread Safety
topics.summary: Thread safety means concurrent operations preserve an object’s invariants and return valid results under the object’s shared-state access patterns.

title: System Design
description: Design for scale, failure, and clear operational guarantees across distributed components.

topics.title: System Design: From Requirements to Architecture
topics.summary: A repeatable system-design process turns an ambiguous product request into a testable architecture and explicit trade-offs.

topics.title: Capacity Estimation: Traffic, Storage & Latency
topics.summary: Back-of-the-envelope estimates translate product usage into rough traffic, storage, bandwidth, and capacity requirements.

topics.title: HLD Case Study: URL Shortener
topics.summary: A URL shortener maps a compact key to a destination and redirects reads quickly while protecting key uniqueness and abuse boundaries.

topics.title: Scalable E-Commerce Order API
topics.summary: Design checkout as a durable, idempotent workflow that preserves inventory and payment invariants while downstream work scales independently.

topics.title: Redis Distributed Caching
topics.summary: A shared Redis cache can reduce repeated source reads across service instances, provided the system deliberately manages stale values, misses, and cache failure.

topics.title: Distributed Rate Limiting
topics.summary: A distributed rate limiter applies shared request quotas across service replicas while controlling bursts and protecting downstream capacity.

topics.title: LLD Case Study: Inventory Reservation
topics.summary: Low-level design turns a business operation into explicit domain objects, contracts, state transitions, and concurrency invariants.

title: Gen AI (.NET)
description: Build .NET AI applications with governed retrieval, model routing, controlled tools, and safe streaming.

topics.title: Prompting, Streaming & Guardrails
topics.summary: Prompts define task context, streaming delivers partial output, and guardrails reduce risks through input, output, and resource controls.

topics.title: LLM Function & Tool Calling
topics.summary: Tool calling lets a model propose a structured request; trusted application code decides whether and how to execute it.

topics.title: RAG Architecture in .NET
topics.summary: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) retrieves relevant authorized material at request time and supplies it to a language model as context.

topics.title: Multi-Model AI Gateway
topics.summary: A model gateway is an application boundary that applies policy and routes model requests to one or more approved deployments.
